title: Cu3PdxN nanocrystals for efficient CO2 electrochemical reduction to methane
abstract: Developing catalysts with high faradaic efficiency and durability for advanced products is a critical issue for ensuring commercial application of CO 2 electrochemical reduction reaction. In this study, a series of Cu 3 Pd x N nanoparticles are developed by one-pot organic phase synthesis and the compositiondependent performance for CO 2 electrochemical reduction reaction is systematically investigated. The highest faradaic efficiency towards methane generation can reach 57.5% on Cu 3 Pd 0.62 N nanoparticles at -1.25 V vs the reversible hydrogen electrode. Moreover, the high faradaic efficiency of methane can be maintained during the 4 h continuous electrolysis. Our results indicate that the appropriate content of Pd could enhance the selectivity of methane and improve the stability of the catalysts. © 2021 Elsevier Ltd. All rights reserved.

Developing catalysts with high faradaic efficiency and durability for advanced products is a critical is-
sue for ensuring commercial application of CO 2 electrochemical reduction reaction. In this study, a series of Cu 3 Pd x N nanoparticles are developed by one-pot organic phase synthesis and the compositiondependent performance for CO 2 electrochemical reduction reaction is systematically investigated. The highest faradaic efficiency towards methane generation can reach 57.5% on Cu 3 Pd 0.62 N nanoparticles at -1.25 V vs the reversible hydrogen electrode. Moreover, the high faradaic efficiency of methane can be
maintained during the 4 h continuous electrolysis. Our results indicate that the appropriate content of Pd
could enhance the selectivity of methane and improve the stability of the catalysts.

. Introduction
The combustion of fossil fuel releases large quantities of carbon
ioxide, causing a severe climate change. In recent years, raised
oncerns on energy and environment-related issues have driven
ignificant efforts on CO 2 conversion technologies. Among them, O 2 electrochemical reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) is considered to e one of the most promising technologies [1–11] . The biggest
hallenge in CO 2 RR is the low performance of the electrocataysts including low product selectivity, reaction rate, and stabil-
ty. Thus, advanced electrocatalysts with a high selectivity of de-
ired products and long term durability for CO 2 RR are urgently eeded. In recent years, high faradaic efficiencies (FE) over 90%
ere achieved for some primary products including CO and for-
ate [12–15] . However, selectively generating advanced products
uch as methane, ethylene, alcohols are still challenging [16–19] .
ethane is one of the main advanced products in CO 2 RR on Cu-
ased catalytsts and also an important chemical feedstock and

Cu-Pd bimetallic catalysts are versatile in generating vari-
us products during CO 2 RR. For instance, Pd 85 Cu 15 nanoparticles 29] , mesoporous Pd 7 Cu 3 [30] , and ordered Pd 3 Cu nanoparticles 31] could efficiently convert CO 2 to CO, while PdCl 2 modified Cu lectrode [32] and phase-separated PdCu nanoparticles [31] mainly
enerated C 2 + products. Cu-Pd was also found as a promising comination for methane generation. For instance, concave rhombic
odecahedral PdCu 3 nanoparticles can generate methane with 40% E at maximum, which lowered the overpotential by 0.4 V as com-
ared to a pure Cu foil [27] . Systematic tuning the composition of
u-Pd alloys can maximize the FE of methane to 51% on PdCu 2 33] . In addition to the bimetallic effects, introducing nitrogen
toms in Cu was also reported as an effective method in improv-
ng the CO 2 -to-methane conversion performance. For instance, the
ethane selectivity of Cu-N composite catalysts was doubled as
ompared to that of Cu 2 O [34] . Combined experiments and density unctional theory (DFT) calculations also demonstrated that the in-
roduction of nitrogen into Cu could improve the catalytic stabil-
ty [35] . In this study, we considered the combination of alloy-
ng and N incorporation effects in improving the catalytic selectiv-

. Experimental
.1. Catalysts synthesis
.1.1. Chemicals
Copper nitrate trihydrate (Cu(NO 3 ) 2 • 3H 2 O) (99%) and 1- ctadecene (90%) were purchased from Aladdin. Palladium(II) 2,4-
entanedionate (Pd(acac) 2 ) (Pd 34.7%) was purchased from Alfa esar. Oleylamine (70%), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and phenol
ere purchased from Sigma-Aldrich. Ethanol (99.8%) and n-hexane
97%) were purchased from VWR Chemicals. Acetone (99.5%) was
urchased from Scharlau. D 2 O was purchased from J&K Chemical.
.1.2. Synthesis of Cu 3 Pd x N nanocrystals
The synthesis procedure of Cu 3 Pd x N nanocrystals was modified rom a previous report [36] . Cu 3 Pd x N nanoparticles with differnt ratio of Cu:Pd were synthesized by changing the quantities of
d(acac) 2 precursor while keeping that of Cu(NO 3 ) 2 • 3H 2 O fixed. In typical synthesis, 160 mg of Cu(NO 3 ) 2 • 3H 2 O and 8.4 mg, 33.6 mg, r 50.4 mg of Pd(acac) 2 were added into the mixture of 6.6 mL of leylamine and 20 mL of 1-octadecene by magnetic stirring. The
olution was then heated to 110 °C and kept for 20 min to remove ater and oxygen. Next, the solution was further heated to 245 °C t a heating rate of ~20 °C min −1 . After 20 min of reaction, the ask was fastly cooled to the room temperature by a water bath
nd the product was precipitated by adding ethanol. Finally, the
roduct was washed with acetone/hexane (4:1) for two times and
ollected by centrifuge at 12,0 0 0 rpm.
.2. Physical characterizations
The morphology and size of the as-synthesized nanoparticles
ere characterized by transmission electron microscope (TEM)
hich was performed on a JEM 2010F microscope operating at
n accelerating voltage of 120 kV. High resolution TEM (HRTEM),
igh angle annular dark-field (HAADF), and energy-dispersive X-
ay spectroscopy (EDS) mapping using an FEI Talos F200X micro-
cope operating at 200 kV were applied to analyze the atomic
tructure and element distribution of the samples. X-ray diffrac-
ion (XRD) patterns were obtained using Phillips PW1830 pow-
er X-ray diffractometer equipped with a Cu Ka radiation source
wavelength: 1.5406 Å) and graphite monochromator. The actual
u to Pd ratio was calculated based on the inductively coupled
lasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES, Optima 7300 DV,
erkinElmer) results after dissolving the catalysts with aqua regia.
-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) characteriztions were per-
ormed on an Axis Ultra DLD multitechnique surface analysis sys-
em.
.3. Electrochemical measurements and products analysis
To prepare the working electrode, 1 mg of Cu 3 Pd x N nanoparicles were mixed with 30 μL of 5 wt% Nafion solution and 500 L of methanol. The suspension was ultrasonicated for more than
hour to get a homogeneous ink. 40 μL of the as-prepared ink
as loaded on a glassy carbon with a diameter of 10 mm and nat-
rally dried. To measure the CO 2 reduction reaction performance f as-synthesized catalysts, potentiostatic electrolysis was applied
nd all the electrochemical measurements were carried out in an
-type cell. The anode and cathode chambers were separated by
Nafion 117 membrane and 30 ml of 0.5 M KHCO 3 solution was dded into each chamber as the electrolyte. A 10 × 10 mm platnum mesh was used as the counter electrode and an Ag/AgCl elec-
rode was used as the reference electrode. All the electrochemi-
al measurements were carried out by an electrochemical work-
tation (CHI 627E, CH Instruments) with the IR dropped automati-
ally compensated (85% compensation level). All the potentials re-
orted are referred to the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). Be-
ore CO 2 RR, CO 2 was purged into both chambers for at least 30 min o saturate the electrolyte and remove residual air. The CO 2 RR perormance was evaluated by potentiostatic electrolysis for at least
hour at certain potentials with continuously purged CO 2 at a ow rate of 30 sccm controlled by a mass flow controller. The elec-
rolyte was stirred at 1500 rpm. The outlet of the cathode chamber
as connected to an online gas chromatography (GC2060, Ramiin)
quipped with a flame ionization detector (FID) to detect gas phase
roducts of CO 2 RR and a thermal conductivity detector (TCD) to etect H 2 from hydrogen evolution reaction. The gas phase prodcts were sampled every 13 min and the average current of 30 s
efore the sampling was adopted for calculating the FE. The liquid
roducts were analyzed by using a Varian 500 MHz nuclear mag-
etic resonance (NMR) spectrometer. To prepare the sample for the
MR test, 450 μL of the post-reaction electrolyte was mixed with 0 μL of 0.5 mM phenol and 0.1 mM DMSO solution (dissolved in 2 O).

n Pd-Cu systems, the Pd sites tended to form Pd-H species. Thus

. Conclusion
In this study, a series of Cu 3 Pd x N nanocrystals were syntheized with a quasicubic morphology. A higher content of Pd led
o a smaller particle size and more regular morphology. All the
ynthesized Cu 3 Pd x N nanocrystals exhibited considerably high FE or methane generation during the CO 2 RR. The maximum FE of
ethane reached 57.5% at −1.25 V on Cu 3 Pd 0.62 N. In addition to good FE of methane, the long-term durability of Cu 3 Pd 0.62 N as also achieved with only 12.7% drop (from 56.9% to 46.7%)
f methane FE after 4 h operation. The HRTEM, STEM-HAADF,
nd EDS element mapping results confirmed that there was no
ignificant morphology and composition change occurred to the
u 3 Pd 0.62 N nanoparticles during CO 2 RR. This study demonstrated hat Cu 3 Pd x N nanocrystals could convert CO 2 to methane effecively and offered new insights in boosting CO 2 RR performance.
